node: Hyperscaler and cloud AI compute demand
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct US-listed universe for the demand node to five companies whose public disclosures or reported contracts show direct exposure to AI compute consumption, AI-cloud capacity buildout, or hyperscale infrastructure demand. This pass prioritizes asset owners and platforms rather than upstream component suppliers. The highest-directness candidates are cloud/hyperscaler platforms and AI cloud capacity sellers; key evidence to validate next is capex guidance, AI-cloud backlog/RPO, utilization, customer concentration, depreciation, financing needs, and whether AI revenue grows fast enough to absorb infrastructure buildout. This Layer 1B pass expands the AI hyperscaler demand node toward less-obvious US-listed suppliers tied to physical deployment chokepoints: electrical/mechanical construction labor, medium-voltage switchgear, liquid cooling, rack-level power/cooling, and AI data-center hardware manufacturing. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. The strongest direct bottleneck signals in this pass are rising data-center backlog/orders at specialty contractors and switchgear vendors, plus explicit vendor moves into liquid cooling for high-density AI racks. Expanded the universe around less-obvious public beneficiaries of hyperscaler/neocloud AI compute demand. The strongest second-order mappings in this pass are not GPU vendors but enabling infrastructure: backup/onsite power, high-density cooling, electrical distribution/logistics, and mechanical/electrical construction.
